name: Relative equal highs / lows (REH / REL)

definitions.definition_text: When swing highs are real close to one another, that is relative equal highs. Lecture asks how to know a high-probability relative equal high likely to get swept; distinguishes from other highs (filter discussed but partially teased).
conditions: Swing highs (or lows) in close proximity
Used as liquidity objectives likely to be swept / traded through
definitions.variations_note: Definitional proximity idea; probability filter details incomplete in extracted cues — do not invent filter.

definitions.definition_text: Prior to the pre-market range, look for equal highs or equal lows — which side has it becomes bias draw. If both relative equal high and relative equal low: wait for the first one to get disrupted, then work to the other — that is your bias. Whichever side has relative equals (smooth area) will be disrupted.
conditions: Scan left of / prior to the 30m pre-market window
Bias from the side that has relative equals; if both, wait for first disruption
invalidation: Ambiguous when both sides present until first disruption occurs
definitions.variations_note: Operational bias rule tied to pre-market range — keep linked but separate from REH geometry definition.

definitions.definition_text: Equal highs act as the contrary liquidity pool (buy stops) after sell-side stops below an old low are accumulated — draw equal highs forward as the opposing pool target.
conditions: After SSL raid / long accumulation below old low
definitions.variations_note: Pool-target use of equal highs — complements pre-market REH bias teaching.
